# Events and timing {#sec-events}

Whatever biyos has to say, a message, a failed check or the time a phase took, it sends as an event on the environment's stream; it writes nothing to standard output or standard error. A program decides what to do with each event by attaching a function to it, a hook. Logging, timing and debugging are this one mechanism. When nobody listens, an event is not even built. The code of this chapter is `examples/c/events.c` and `examples/python/events.py`.

## Kinds and levels {#sec-events-kinds}

Every event has a kind and a level:

| Kind | Carries |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `BIYOS_EVT_MESSAGE` | a message: a level, the module that sent it, a text and fields |
| `BIYOS_EVT_CHECK` | a failed check: the invariant that does not hold, the object it was checked on and the values involved |
| `BIYOS_EVT_PHASE` | a phase beginning or ending, with the wall and CPU time |

The levels, from least to most severe, are `BIYOS_LVL_DBG`, `BIYOS_LVL_INFO`, `BIYOS_LVL_WARN` and `BIYOS_LVL_ERR`; a larger value is more severe. An event also has the name of the module that sent it, such as `capi` or `core`, a text and a list of fields, each a name and a value, both text.

## Hooks {#sec-events-hooks}

A hook is a function of the event and of a pointer the program chose, of type `BIYOS_hook`. `BIYOS_addenvhook` attaches it to one kind of event at a lowest level, and it then receives every event of that kind at that level or a more severe one. This helper adds a hook on messages:

```{.c file="examples/c/events.c" item="hook"}
```

The call writes an id for the hook, and `BIYOS_delenvhook` removes it by that id. Ids count from 1 in each environment and are never reused. The hooks of an environment receive an event in the order they were added. biyos keeps the function and the pointer until the hook is removed or the environment is freed, and passes the pointer back as given, so it may be null.

The example adds three hooks and then makes a call fail:

```{.c file="examples/c/events.c" item="main"}
```

## Formatting an event {#sec-events-format}

Two calls write an event as one line, for people or for tools. They work like `snprintf`, with one difference in order: the caller gives the size of a buffer first and the buffer after it, as every call takes its inputs before its outputs. The call writes as much of the line as fits, followed by a NUL, and `len` receives the length of the whole line. A size of 0 writes nothing and only reports the length, so a hook can size its buffer exactly:

```{.c file="examples/c/events.c" item="print_json"}
```

`BIYOS_fmttext` writes the time, the level, the module, the text and the fields; `BIYOS_fmtjson` writes one JSON object with the members `time`, `kind`, `level`, `module`, `text` and `fields`. The failed call of the example gives lines like these, the time aside:

```text
0.000125 error capi: invalid argument: option 'seed': -1 is outside [0, 2147483647] code=-100
{"time":0.000125,"kind":"message","level":"error","module":"capi","text":"invalid argument: option 'seed': -1 is outside [0, 2147483647]","fields":{"code":"-100"}}
```

The time is the wall time since the environment was created, in seconds with six decimals, whatever the locale. A line never holds a line break: a byte below 0x20 is written as an escape such as `\n`. JSON output is always valid: bytes that are not well-formed UTF-8 become U+FFFD there, while text output passes them through.

## Reading an event {#sec-events-read}

A hook can also read the parts of an event one by one, with `BIYOS_getevtknd`, `BIYOS_getevtlvl`, `BIYOS_getevtmod`, `BIYOS_getevttext`, `BIYOS_getnevtfld` and the field readers. These calls cannot fail: a null event or a field number out of range gives 0 or an empty string. This function finds the status code an error message carries:

```{.c file="examples/c/events.c" item="code_of"}
```

## The events biyos sends {#sec-events-sent}

Two messages exist so far. A call that fails sends an error message, at level error from module `capi`, whose text is the call's error message and whose one field `code` is the returned status as decimal text, so a hook sees every failure without checking every call. Setting a deprecated option sends a warning from module `core` (@sec-options-versions).

A check event reports an invariant that does not hold, found by a check that the option `check_lvl` runs; the call then fails. A phase event marks a phase beginning or ending, such as presolve, and phases nest. The fields of a phase event, `edge`, `wall` and `cpu`, give `begin` or `end` and the wall time since the environment was created and the CPU time of the process, both in nanoseconds. biyos adds up the time of each phase in a timing tree, nested as the phases are, and leaves out the time spent delivering phase events, so a hook never changes it. @sec-codes describes each event field by field.

::: {.callout-note}
## Not yet sent
No call runs a check or times a phase yet: these events arrive with the solvers.
:::

## Inside a hook {#sec-events-inside}

While a hook runs, its environment is delivering an event and is read-only, together with the models made on it. The hook may read options, the last error message, the event and the models. A call that would change the environment or one of its models, setting an option, adding or removing a hook, creating, changing or freeing a model, fails with `BIYOS_ERR_BADARG` and changes nothing. Such a failure keeps its message, so `BIYOS_lasterror` explains it, but sends no event, and when the hook returns the last error is again what it was before. The event and every string read from it are valid only until the hook returns.

## Events in Python {#sec-events-python}

In Python, `env.addhook` attaches any callable that takes one `Event` and returns an id for `env.delhook`. The event's properties, such as `kind`, `level` and `text`, read its parts, and `fmttext` and `fmtjson` give its lines. Forwarding events to Python's `logging` module takes a few lines:

```{.python file="examples/python/events.py"}
```

An exception raised by a hook does not escape into C. biyos keeps the first one and raises it in the program once the call that sent the event returns, in place of any error of the call itself. The event is valid only while the hook runs: reading it afterwards raises `ValueError`.
